subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, bearing inscriptions in Common, Dwarven, and a reference to Stroudite chess symbolism.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription. The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher affiliated with the Order of the Gauntlet and personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing off on its creation.
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Common. *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.* Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, possibly including Stroudite members, though the priest declined to confirm specifics.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet endorsed the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel personally witnessing its creation, and now sells pewter replicas of the arm as charitable donations.
source_quote: The priest was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, and he was clearly delighted with his own enterprise.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and subsequent martyrdom.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: A bronze monument to Tarvis Ulain, depicting his severed forearm, was erected in Daggerford’s market square two years after his death, bearing layered inscriptions that reference both Bahamutian devotion and Stroudite symbolism.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: pewter hand cast
fact: Pewter miniature replicas of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm are being sold by a village priest as charitable donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, measuring charm-sized and not full size.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway... carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain is mounted on a stone pillar in Daggerford’s market square, bearing three inscriptions: Common (identifying Tarvis), Dwarven (*The move is yours.*), and Common (*Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.*).
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite chess reference (*The move is yours.*) appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, raising questions about religious syncretism, tolerance, or hidden alliances in post-war Daggerford.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: priest's ambiguous tolerance
fact: The village priest claims to be a 'pure Bahamutian' but allows a Stroudite inscription to remain on the monument, citing it as a 'gift' that should not be removed, suggesting deeper political or theological compromises.
source_quote: It was a gift,' he said finally. 'And since it was a gift, we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?'

subject: Daggerford's silent trauma
fact: Daggerford bears visible markers of war — the monument, the pewter relics, the lingering tension over religious symbolism — yet avoids open discussion of its pain, mirroring the unspoken silence observed by the party upon arrival.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... Townfolk walked around something none of them would point at. Nobody explained why.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut who notices and questions the layered symbolism of the monument, purchases a pewter hand cast, and presses the priest for theological clarity, revealing his role as an investigator of hidden truths.
source_quote: Grygum looked at them. 'Are they full size?'... Grygum dropped a gold piece in for his... Grygum asked him to tell him more... 'As am I,' Grygum said. 'But the inscription shares language with Stroud. Why is that?'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a dwarf who reads and interprets the Dwarven inscription on the monument, recognizes the Stroudite chess reference, and confirms its accuracy due to his linguistic fluency in Dwarven.
source_quote: Daz was already reading the inscription... Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*... I read it twice because Dwarven is, you know, actually my language, or one of them, and I wanted to make sure I hadn't misread. I hadn't.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is a destination in Daggerford where the party ultimately arrives after observing the monument and encountering the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: Daggerford market square
fact: The market square in Daggerford is the site of Tarvis Ulain’s bronze forearm monument and the center of the priest’s sales activity, symbolizing the town’s attempt to memorialize trauma through public art and commerce.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm... Daz was already reading the inscription... The priest was selling them for donations...

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a southern town in the North that avoided the worst of the Uthgardt hordes but suffered the Cult of the Dragon’s incursion, losing Tarvis Ulain and now memorializing him with contested religious symbolism.
source_quote: Daggerford had been far enough south to miss the Uthgardt barbarian hordes... They'd only gotten the cult. Only lost Tarvis.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, and the monument to him was funded two years after his death, placing the current events approximately one year after the monument’s unveiling.
source_quote: The primary text told us this was Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years... The whole thing was funded two years after the war...

subject: two years post-war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument two years after the war, situating its creation in the early recovery phase of Daggerford’s post-conflict society.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin is a 7-year-old girl who has been silent for six days, draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface in her environment, and speaks only in her sleep — her utterance being 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: She says it is only the shape that holds.

subject: Maerith of the Ford
fact: Maerith is Elin’s mother, exhausted from seeking help at every temple and institution, and has repeatedly been turned away — she noticed the dragon-and-scale holy symbol as the usual trigger for hope.
source_quote: She spotted my holy symbol during dinner, which is the usual trigger.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a meticulous observer with a precise mind, who noticed subtle environmental and perceptual anomalies others dismissed — including a growing pressure in his own head.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the mechanism of Elin’s condition as a perceptual distortion — the world is arriving as corrupted audio input she cannot process, not as magic or disease.
source_quote: The input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword with strong opinions on timing and intervention; it initiated Lesser Restoration on Elin, which enabled her first coherent speech.
source_quote: Let me bring the light to you.

subject: The Underdark’s Structural Wrongness
fact: An emergent, non-magical corruption originating beneath the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and reality processing in those it touches — manifesting as auditory hallucinations and symbolic withdrawal.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below.

subject: The Temples
fact: The temples have been unable to diagnose or treat Elin’s condition, reflecting their institutional limitations against non-magical, non-infectious perceptual corruption.
source_quote: The temples have no answer.

subject: Lesser Restoration on Elin
fact: A Lesser Restoration spell cast by Dawnbringer cleared enough mental interference for Elin to speak one coherent sentence — 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Perceptual Distortion Diagnosis
fact: The party concluded that Elin’s condition is not a disease, infection, or magical effect, but a perceptual failure — the world is transmitting corrupted signals she cannot interpret, resulting in silence and symbolic repetition.
source_quote: It wasn't a disease in the conventional sense. It was more like the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process.

subject: Six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s repeated drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are not random — they are an attempt to externalize and stabilize an internal perceptual collapse.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: The Wells Are Not Wells Anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance is a cryptic revelation pointing to a fundamental distortion in reality — 'wells' may symbolize sources of perception, truth, or connection that have been corrupted or replaced.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: The Pressure in Daz’s Head
fact: Daz’s unacknowledged head pressure suggests he is experiencing the same perceptual bleed as Elin — a sign the corruption is spreading and may be active in others.
source_quote: I looked at him. I looked at Elin. I thought about what we'd just established.

subject: The Bleeding Underdark
fact: The structural wrongness from beneath is not contained — it is rising, affecting perception across the surface world, and may be the root cause of recent phenomena in Neverlight Grove, the Pudding King’s court, and now Elin.
source_quote: It was reaching up. It was reaching Elin.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during a single night of medical and metaphysical inquiry — the culmination of failed temple visits, failed examinations, and a final revelation.
source_quote: Twenty-three. My best of the evening, arriving too late to be medically useful and just in time to be philosophically concerning.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who catalogues environments unconsciously, noting exits, patterns, and deviations from baseline behavior; he recently observed a young scholar misrendering a liturgical chant with a degradation pattern matching two prior cases of cognitive decay.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar with a performative interest in Stroud, who maps thematic motifs from bardic songs onto historical figures like Whistler, and accepts theological downgrades with bureaucratic precision.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign, involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: The Young Human Scholar
fact: A young human scholar in the corner of The Burning Wizard Inn is reciting a liturgical chant with a precise, non-beginner-level degradation pattern — identical to the cognitive distortions previously observed in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher.
source_quote: His breathing was almost right. The pauses fell almost correctly. The pattern was almost the one it was supposed to be — and wrong by a hair in a way that took actual knowledge of the correct version to notice.

subject: The Traveling Bard
fact: A traveling bard performs seasonal songs with thematic resonance — including 'The Kenku Could Not Fly' — and adapts her repertoire in response to patrons' holy symbols, translating grand theological narratives into accessible folk metaphors.
source_quote: She took the coin and proceeded to sing a love song. Involving flowers. And drinking.

subject: Festrum
fact: Festrum, the ancient gnome innkeeper of The Burning Wizard Inn, maintains the physical memory of a wizard's death by refusing to paint the wall where he fell, and scrubs the floor seasonally as ritual observance.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a site of layered memory — its architecture preserves the death of a wizard burned by a dragon cult, and its atmosphere hosts recurring patterns of ritual degradation, bardic reinterpretation, and scholarly observation.
source_quote: The inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued.

subject: Demon Lords
fact: Demon lords are actively broadcasting — rewriting the language of wells, shapes, and held things — and finding new listeners, suggesting an ongoing, insidious linguistic corruption affecting perception and cognition.
source_quote: Somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting, still finding new listeners, still rewriting the language of wells and shapes and held things into something the surface world hadn't been built to receive.

subject: Chant Degradation Pattern
fact: A specific, non-random degradation pattern in a liturgical chant has been observed in three individuals — the young scholar, Eldred, and the Field Ward Preacher — indicating a possible contagion, doctrinal corruption, or targeted cognitive assault.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: Cognitive Contagion
fact: A recurring, identifiable distortion in ritual chanting may be a symptom of a broader, unexplained phenomenon — possibly tied to demon lord broadcasts or a hidden heresy — that has afflicted at least three people and may be spreading.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice.

subject: Daz's Journal
fact: Daz's journal contains precise transcriptions of the malformed chant cadence, including syncopation errors and syllabic deviations — data he intends to cross-reference with Candlekeep’s archives to determine if this is a known doctrine or an emerging corruption.
source_quote: Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: Bahamutians
fact: Bahamutians, including Grygum, maintain a sentimentality for other faiths like Stroud’s, but interpret theological narratives through a lens of disciplined restraint and bureaucratic translation, often reducing grand stakes to pragmatic or folkloric forms.
source_quote: He explained that he was Bahamutian, with sentimentality for the other.

subject: Stroudites
fact: Stroudites are associated with intellectual traditions — particularly chess as metaphor — and are referenced in bardic songs as figures of strategic depth, though their theological grandeur is frequently flattened into romantic allegory by outsiders.
source_quote: Grygum leaned forward — he has a scholar's interest in Stroud that he performs slightly harder than the interest actually requires — and offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: Day of Observation
fact: The day of observation was unusually long in sunlight exposure — the first time in a while Daz had been outside in the sun this long — which he initially misattributed as the source of his cognitive friction.
source_quote: I had been attributing the sensation to sunlight. I had, in fact, been attributing it to sunlight for most of the day.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Brother Khell-Vire as his handler, having previously meditated on the roof and resolved an internal argument about the nature of wisdom and delay.
source_quote: Hmm, true,

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Master Archivist Philemon; he processed the group’s ethical dilemma by talking to Glabbagool and concluded the ooze was ambivalent about its role as a jailer.
source_quote: You just gotta go with it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Vareth; he was the one who first noted the connection between Daz’s distress and the spreading madness from the Underdark, and summarized the group’s capture as: "We've been caught."
source_quote: We've been caught.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz arrived at Candlekeep and was assigned to Sister Yvenne; he became unusually quiet during the walk, touching his temple, and exhibited signs of the spreading madness from the Underdark that had not ceased at the surface.

subject: The Spy (House T'sarran)
fact: The spy, a miniaturized operative of House T'sarran, was discovered in the group’s bag at Candlekeep’s gate; she demanded formal imprisonment and was furious when told her fate was not hers to decide, but she had become an unwilling companion to Glabbagool.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a grey ooze, was carried in the same bag as the spy and had spent days observing and interacting with her; he claimed they had become great friends through repeated attempts at murder, escape, meditation, and conversation, and asked Zalthir whether this made him more or less of a monk.
source_quote: Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her?

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, Gate Warden of Candlekeep, reviewed the group’s violation of protocol regarding the spy and delivered Candlekeep’s official stance: that prisoners are not kept, only delayed, and that the spy would be released eventually with a warning.
source_quote: What you are giving us is a delay.

subject: Bookwyrm (First Reader)
fact: Bookwyrm, a dragonborn sage and First Reader of Candlekeep, assigned each member of the party to a handler without ceremony and recognized the spy’s presence as a breach of protocol, but deferred judgment on her status to the party’s discretion.
source_quote: The decision was ours, not hers.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep maintains a strict policy against imprisonment: those found guilty of major offenses are exiled rather than jailed, and prisoners are only held temporarily as a delay, never as a sentence; the institution values knowledge, order, and restraint over punishment.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a secretive and powerful organization that deploys miniaturized spies; it seeks the return or elimination of its operative captured by the party, and is treated as an external threat by Candlekeep.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze, was carried in the group’s bag alongside the spy and demonstrated unusual cognitive behavior: he engaged in prolonged interaction with her, attempted to teach meditation, and expressed philosophical uncertainty about his own nature as a monk.
source_quote: I've been doing prison-watching, and was kind of bored.

subject: The Bag
fact: The bag contained both Glabbagool and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy; its contents were revealed at Candlekeep’s gate, triggering a protocol breach and forcing the party to confront the ethical implications of carrying a living prisoner and a monster together.
source_quote: We've been caught.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a vast, ancient library-fortress visible for miles along the Sea of Swords; it sits as a dark stack of towers against the sky, embodying centuries of accumulated knowledge and rigid institutional tradition.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The party arrived at Candlekeep after traveling from the Underdark; their bag’s contents were discovered, triggering a formal review by the Gate Warden, assignments by the First Reader, and the beginning of a moral and institutional standoff over the spy’s fate.
source_quote: We gave them the books at the gate.

subject: the spy’s fate
fact: The fate of the House T'sarran spy remains unresolved: Candlekeep refuses to execute or imprison her, but will not release her immediately; the party must decide whether to accept a delay, intervene, or abandon her — a question that echoes the difference between solutions and postponements.
source_quote: What you are giving us is a delay.

subject: Glabbagool’s monkhood
fact: Glabbagool’s interaction with the spy has raised a metaphysical question: whether watching and engaging with a prisoner constitutes spiritual growth or moral corruption; Zalthir affirmed it as pre-monk training, but the nature of that training remains ambiguous.
source_quote: Absolutely.

subject: the spreading madness
fact: Daz’s uncharacteristic silence and distress suggest the Underdark’s spreading madness has followed the party to Candlekeep; its origin, mechanism, and target remain unknown, and it may be more than mere psychological trauma.
source_quote: Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during the party’s arrival at Candlekeep, following their journey from the Underdark; the exact calendar date is unrecorded, but the temporal context is marked by the transition from subterranean chaos to institutional stillness.

subject: the wall of the inn
fact: The soot mark on the south wall of the inn remained unchanged, a silent witness to repeated comings and goings; its persistence symbolized the endurance of place over transient human concerns.
source_quote: The wall remembers.

subject: the inn’s bar
fact: Festrum wiped the bar, a ritual of maintenance that echoed Candlekeep’s own routines; the bar, like the wall, bore the marks of time and repetition, a place of quiet constancy.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who disregarded formal training in favor of practical survival in the Underdark; he executes techniques unconventionally but effectively, prioritizing results over doctrinal correctness.
source_quote: He had survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elven shadow monk lineage keeper who evaluates students not on what they know, but on what they have become through lived experience; he operates outside traditional pedagogical frameworks.
source_quote: He was asking what Zalthir had become through what he'd lived.

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The Blind Monk is a senior shadow monk evaluator who enforces canonical techniques but is forced to acknowledge superior efficacy in unorthodox methods; he represents institutional dogma confronted by adaptive mastery.
source_quote: You skip the third breath... It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: Shadow Discipline Lineage
fact: The Shadow Discipline Lineage is a centuries-old monastic tradition within Candlekeep that maintains rigid records and formalized techniques, yet is being challenged by practitioners like Zalthir whose lived experience supersedes documented doctrine.
source_quote: The Shadow Discipline Lineage Records were kept... stretching back five centuries.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir's trial was a structured evaluation designed to test adherence to shadow monk orthodoxy, but it instead revealed the limitations of institutional assessment when confronted with unconventional, survival-based mastery.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Echoing Hall (Candlekeep's North Inner Ward)
fact: The Echoing Hall is a stone-walled corridor in Candlekeep's inner ward known for distorting and reflecting sound in ways that suggest the architecture itself is recording or interpreting speech — a metaphor for the trial’s deeper purpose.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Note on Khell-Vire's Desk
fact: The note — 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings' — is an enigmatic directive with no known origin, serving as a cryptic trigger for the trial’s philosophical inquiry into meaning, memory, and lived experience.
source_quote: Neither of them could place it. I filed it under 'questions to revisit' and did not volunteer an opinion, because I didn't have one.

subject: The Curriculum Divide
fact: The central unresolved thread is whether formal monastic training and survival-based adaptation are mutually exclusive, or if one is merely a subset of the other — a question neither institution nor individual can fully answer.
source_quote: There's a case to be made that those are the same thing. There's also a case that they're almost never the same thing.

subject: The Bone King
fact: The Bone King is an unseen, mythic entity referenced in cryptic directives and monastic prophecy; his arrival is a temporal marker of unknown significance, possibly tied to the collapse or transformation of shadow monk traditions.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: session date
fact: The trial occurred during an unspecified but internally significant session in Candlekeep’s inner ward, marked not by calendar date but by the weight of accumulated tradition and the rupture of Zalthir’s unorthodox performance.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-optimized individual who ignored the manual, built an unconventional shadow technique through improvisation, and impressed the blind monk Khell-Vire with a 29-to-hit strike that shattered a thrown brick — demonstrating that his unorthodox approach is more effective than traditional training.
source_quote: I rolled a 29 to hit. The brick did not survive.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a blind monk who initially judged Zalthir’s skills as weak and untrained, but ultimately recognized that Zalthir’s combination of shadow step and strike — not his individual mechanics — revealed a deeper, forgotten lineage of shadow monks, and awarded him a specialized technique as a result.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a companion who advocates for Dawnbringer’s personhood, insists on using gendered pronouns for a sentient blade, and seeks validation for the emotional bond formed through shared trauma — challenging institutional dehumanization of magical artifacts.
source_quote: What do you mean, specimen? This is my friend Dawnbringer.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient, late Netherese-era blade forged in sun-worship, subjected to three to four millennia of darkness, and now recognized by Thorin as a person — capable of companionship, identity, and emotional reciprocity despite lacking a conventional body.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... we've gotten to know each other pretty well over the last stressful ordeals.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an archivist trained to view magical artifacts as specimens, but he paused and reset his assumptions when confronted with Thorin’s insistence on Dawnbringer’s personhood — indicating a latent openness to redefining classification beyond institutional norms.
source_quote: He looked up. There was a pause. The kind where someone resets the question in their head before they say the next thing.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are an ancient, possibly lost lineage of warriors who mastered discrete movement over brute strikes — their methods forgotten until Zalthir’s untrained combination of shadow step and attack inadvertently resurrected their principles.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Gelatinous Cube Collective
fact: The Gelatinous Cube Collective is a newly emerging sentient entity — once dismissed as mindless — now recognized as a student of the monk path, capable of walking, torturing drows, and learning shadow techniques, with a growing reputation that defies xenobiological assumptions.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking.

subject: Gelatinous Cube
fact: The Gelatinous Cube is a once-mindless ooze now trained in shadow techniques, capable of movement, emotional expression, and recursive learning — its transformation from hazard to student marked by the approval of sages and the production of Resonant Slime.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: Drow Overseer
fact: The Drow Overseer is a captive or subordinate drow being 'tortured' by the Gelatinous Cube — not as a victim, but as part of its training process — indicating a reversal of power dynamics and the emergence of non-traditional mentorship in the Underdark.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: Resonant Slime is a rare alchemical substance produced by the Gelatinous Cube Collective, used to affirm its sentience and legitimacy — its presence signifies institutional recognition of non-human intelligence.
source_quote: The sage... produced a vial of Resonant Slime.

subject: Shadow Tentacles
fact: Shadow Tentacles are an unrecorded, self-developed ability of Zalthir, grown from his eldritch tattoo — a technique outside official manuals, born of improvisation and later validated by Khell-Vire as a legitimate expression of shadow mastery.
source_quote: I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Brick-Shattering Strike
fact: Zalthir’s 29-to-hit strike on a thrown brick resulted in its complete destruction — an unprecedented physical manifestation of shadow power that silenced skepticism and forced reevaluation of combat doctrine.
source_quote: The brick did not survive.

subject: Shadow Step + Strike Combination
fact: Zalthir’s synchronized use of shadow step and melee strike — though individually flawed — produced a result that resonated with ancient shadow monk principles, triggering Khell-Vire’s recognition and the award of a new technique.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: Pronoun of Dawnbringer
fact: The question of whether Dawnbringer is 'he,' 'she,' or 'they' remains unresolved in institutional records — but Thorin’s insistence on personhood has turned it into a living, unresolved ethical thread that challenges archival norms.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... we've gotten to know each other pretty well.

subject: Manual vs. Improvisation
fact: The ongoing conflict between official combat manuals and Zalthir’s self-built techniques continues to produce results that invalidate the manuals — a thread that redefines mastery as creation rather than conformity.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's Study
fact: Philemon’s study is a space of traditional scholarship — smelling of ink and mineral residue — that became the site of a paradigm shift when a sentient blade was recognized not as a specimen but as a person.
source_quote: Smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Candlekeep Libraries
fact: The Candlekeep Libraries are a repository of knowledge that failed to record Zalthir’s innovations or the Gelatinous Cube’s sentience — yet became the destination where these unrecorded phenomena arrived, forcing expansion of the canon.
source_quote: We had not brought a gelatinous cube this far — through the Underdark, through Waterdeep, into the libraries of Candlekeep — to have him dismissed as a mindless digestive system before lunch.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events described occurred during a session where unrecorded character development, improvised mechanics, and emergent sentience were validated by narrative and mechanical outcomes — marking a turning point in how power, identity, and mastery are defined.
source_quote: I filed it under 'Zalthir: things that are not in the records but will be.'

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is not offended by flippant remarks about sentient weapons and has likely heard worse, demonstrating emotional resilience and familiarity with magical artifacts.
source_quote: I understand," Philemon said. He wasn't offended. He'd probably heard worse.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who experiences deep unease from prolonged darkness and disuse, and notices when others speak around her rather than to her.
source_quote: Most people talk around the sword, which she notices.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient magical weapon encountered as a companion and psychological burden, exhibiting emotional responses to environment and ownership, and requiring emotional labor to heal.
source_quote: She can't be polished, actually. She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a named sunblade weapon that requires not physical maintenance but spiritual reconnection to light and emotional mourning for past trauma.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination in Menzoberranzan smells of old stone and residual spell energy, with spectral mage hands drifting between shelves to fetch tomes for researchers who never look up.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates under a strict policy of reciprocal knowledge exchange — every question answered requires a corresponding entry in the ledger, making it a philosophically balanced archive.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Dawnbringer's reconnection to light
fact: Dawnbringer is undergoing a two-stage process: first, reacquainting with daylight without combat, then grieving her past trauma — a ritual initiated by Philemon and accepted by the wielder.
source_quote: We will start with the first.

subject: Headache inquiry at Candlekeep
fact: The narrator attempts to ask about their persistent headache during a formal research session at Candlekeep, but is redirected toward the primary purpose of the inquiry.
source_quote: Can I see or read any of… do any of them… I'm… at this point, my headache… my headache's been bothering me.

subject: The first wielder's identity
fact: The identity of Dawnbringer’s original wielder — the corpse she was found in — remains unspoken but deeply significant, and its unasked question lingers in the silence after Dawnbringer goes quiet.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind.

subject: The giants' saying
fact: The narrator’s childhood giants had a saying: 'the ground under a joker is the same ground everyone else is standing on' — a metaphor for humor as a response to unbearable specificity, now echoed in their own flippant remarks.
source_quote: The giants who raised me had a saying that translated roughly as: the ground under a joker is the same ground everyone else is standing on.

subject: Menzoberranzan's Divination Order
fact: Menzoberranzan's Divination Order maintains the Hall of Divination as a repository of arcane knowledge, where spectral mage hands perform automated retrieval, indicating a culture that treats magic as institutionalized habit.
source_quote: Spectral mage hands drift between the shelves, fetching tomes for researchers who don't look up.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a session in which emotional weight is carried by sentient weapons and archival inquiry, concluding with a lighter note after prolonged darkness.
source_quote: It was a lighter note to end on than the session probably warranted.

subject: The prescription
fact: A prescription is nearly retrieved by Philemon before he catches himself, suggesting an unspoken medical or magical intervention related to Dawnbringer’s condition or the narrator’s distress.
source_quote: He started to reach for a prescription and caught himself mid-sentence.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne is a Candlekeep archivist who manages scholarly inquiries with patient, unwavering adherence to protocol, accustomed to unorthodox requests from overeager researchers.
source_quote: Sister Yvenne looked at me with the particular expression of someone who has spent decades managing scholars and has nevertheless not encountered this exact request.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a place of total, unbroken darkness where Dawnbringer was carried for months, inflicting psychological and magical damage due to absence of light.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Healing work in Waterdeep
fact: The narrator and Dawnbringer performed healing work in Waterdeep by aiding orphans and the sick, allowing Dawnbringer to fulfill her purpose and visibly regain happiness.
source_quote: We'd done the healing work in Waterdeep on the road south, found orphans and the sick and let her do what she was built to do. She'd been visibly happy.

subject: The plus one
fact: The narrator jokingly suggests Dawnbringer will 'grow a plus one' — implying a future companion or evolution — a hopeful, informal closure to a heavy narrative arc.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this," I said. "Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Drow (Player Character)
fact: The drow has no memory of their past, suffers from a persistent headache, and was imprisoned in the Underdark with others before escaping. They are currently in Candlekeep, seeking help and truth, and have no knowledge of their identity or history. They are not lying, but cannot afford the usual drow strategies of concealment.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story. This is the short version. I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us. And we've made an escape. We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada. Now I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Librarian (Menzoberranzan Scholar)
fact: The librarian is a scholar of drow noble houses with access to sealed records. She understands the mechanics of power, betrayal, and record manipulation in Menzoberranzan. She trusts the drow’s honesty despite its deviation from cultural norms and guides them through the hidden logic of the Houses, especially the meaning of 'struck' and the privileges of the fourth seat.
source_quote: Whenever a house sought to destroy another house, it had to destroy everyone. If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit. The wider community would come for you. They would reduce you to a black puddle and call the matter settled.

subject: Menzoberranzan Noble Houses
fact: The noble houses of Menzoberranzan operate under a rigid hierarchy of matron mothers at the top, with power flowing upward and loyalty enforced transactionally. Intrigue is institutionalized: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Houses that fail to eliminate all targets are destroyed by the collective. Record manipulation, especially via the fourth seat’s archive privileges, is a tool of erasure disguised as legitimacy.
source_quote: The rule of intrigue: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Advance through maneuver. The city selects for it.

subject: The Fourth Seat
fact: The Fourth Seat in Menzoberranzan holds ritual archive privileges — the legal authority to access, alter, and erase records. A 'struck' Fourth Seat is not merely politically eliminated; it is an expensive, infrastructural act of systemic erasure requiring knowledge of the right people, payment, and the ability to make the alteration appear as if it never occurred.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: House Erasure Attempt
fact: One noble house attempted to wipe out a rival house but failed to eliminate a single survivor — a blithering child idiot. The house was subsequently destroyed by the wider community. The child’s fate remains officially unknown, and the survivor may be the drow.
source_quote: They had tried to wipe out another, and failed to account for one survivor. A child. A blithering child idiot, she said, and I noted the language was hers, not mine.

subject: The Ledger of Houses
fact: A document listing the noble houses of Menzoberranzan, annotated with terms like 'second seat', 'fourth seat struck', 'eleventh seat', and 'twenty-third seat'. The term 'struck' is distinct from elimination — it implies attempted erasure that failed or was concealed. The document is held in Candlekeep and contains hidden meaning accessible only to those who understand Menzoberranzan's linguistic and bureaucratic codes.
source_quote: She read me the list. The second seat. The fourth seat struck. The eleventh seat. The twenty-third seat. *Struck.*

subject: Candlekeep Library
fact: Candlekeep is a repository of all known knowledge, yet something vital — the record of the struck fourth seat and the true fate of the surviving child — is missing. This absence is not accidental; it is a deliberate, expensive act of censorship that contradicts the library's purpose. The drow perceives this gap as evidence of a powerful manipulation of truth.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation. That is not a small act. That is a very large, very expensive, very deliberate act.

subject: Spider Entity (Underdark Captor)
fact: A mysterious spider-like creature was present in the Underdark prison where the drow and others were held. It appeared to be keeping them contained, possibly as part of a larger scheme. Its nature, allegiance, and current status are unknown. The drow describes it with fragmented, non-technical language, suggesting trauma or memory loss.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: The Struck Fourth Seat
fact: The identity and fate of the house associated with the 'struck' fourth seat remain obscured. The term implies an attempted erasure that did not fully succeed, and the drow suspects they are connected to it — possibly as the sole survivor. The record was altered using archive privileges, and the truth is buried under layers of institutional deception.
source_quote: Struck," I said. "Didn't mean eliminated. It means they struck it, but maybe they didn't eliminate it, and therefore, like, it didn't happen? Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: The Blithering Child Survivor
fact: The identity of the child who survived the house purge is unknown. The drow asks if they are that child — a question the librarian refuses to answer directly. The silence implies the drow may be the survivor, and their memory loss, headache, and presence in Candlekeep are not coincidences but consequences of a cover-up.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: The Sealed Record
fact: There is a house so deeply erased that even the librarian cannot speak of it within the library — because the public record is sealed, and she is the public record. To uncover the truth, the drow must seek it through other doors, suggesting the existence of hidden archives, illicit networks, or non-recorded histories outside Candlekeep’s official collection.
source_quote: There was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: Memory Restoration Trigger
fact: The drow’s headache and fragmented memories began to resolve upon hearing the word 'struck' and understanding its bureaucratic meaning. The recognition of linguistic nuance — not factual recall — triggered a cognitive shift, suggesting their identity and past are encoded in the language of Menzoberranzan’s power structures, not in their personal memory.
source_quote: Something in me landed on it before I could explain why.

subject: Two Years Ago
fact: Two years ago, the drow woke up in a jail cell with no memories and a headache that never left. This is the temporal anchor for their loss of identity and the beginning of their current journey — a point before which their past is inaccessible, and after which they have been navigating a world they no longer recognize.
source_quote: before I woke up in a jail cell with no memories and a headache that apparently never left.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a diminutive form of Daz'issin, a name mothers in Menzoberranzan used for sons they wished to protect, with fewer than a handful of recorded uses in the last three centuries, and associated houses that have all perished.
source_quote: She told me it was a softening name. That mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries. And that the houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a keeper of restricted knowledge in Menzoberranzan, maintaining a pose of neutral informant while her body language — five minutes of practiced stillness contradicting her words — reveals she is carefully navigating what she can say, knowing more than the public record allows.
source_quote: She had been sitting for the last several minutes — the practiced stillness of someone who knows more than the public record allows her to say, maintaining the pose of a person who is simply informing rather than carefully navigating.

subject: Houses that used Daz'issin
fact: The noble houses that historically used the name Daz'issin have all perished, with no known survivors or continuations in the last three centuries, suggesting systematic eradication or collapse.
source_quote: The houses that had those names have all gone.

subject: Heraldry book: *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe*
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text, partially defaced by a deliberate, razor-cut removal of an appendix referenced by a footnote on Daz'issin, indicating intentional suppression of information tied to the name and its lineage.
source_quote: A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Two distinct groups of mercenaries are actively tracking Daz — one to ensure his survival, the other to kill him — suggesting his identity or lineage is of high strategic value and contested between opposing powers.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: Missing appendix on Daz'issin
fact: The appendix referenced in the footnote on Daz'issin has been physically excised from the heraldry book, creating an unresolved gap in the historical record that may contain the truth of Daz's origins, the fate of his house, or the identity of his protector.
source_quote: The appendix was missing.

subject: Silence of Yvenne
fact: Yvenne’s refusal to answer the question 'What if they weren't successfully all gone?' constitutes a deliberate, non-verbal affirmation in Menzoberranzan’s culture — where silence in the ledger is an answer — implying that at least one house or lineage tied to Daz'issin may still endure.
source_quote: She said nothing. Which is, in the ledger, an answer.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where reading rooms, interpreting body language, and recognizing when someone’s posture contradicts their speech are essential survival skills — and where silence, omission, and defaced texts are tools of power and concealment.
source_quote: Menzoberranzan teaches you to read rooms. It teaches you to watch for the moment when someone's body stops matching their words.
